overview: Cross-sectional household survey from January to March 2027 with door-to-door visits and test-button verification of alarms, drawn as a stratified two-stage cluster sample from the county property roll.
population: Occupied residential addresses on the county property roll; one adult householder per address; tenure recorded at the door.
exposure: Housing tenure (privately rented, social rented, owner-occupied) and main heating type (solid fuel, heating oil, bottled gas, heat pump or electric).
procedures: Seventy segments of about 23 addresses each are selected with probability proportional to size within town and rural strata, giving about 1,630 addresses. Fieldworkers in pairs visit up to three times at different times of day. With verbal consent they record alarm presence, siting, manufacture date and whether the alarm sounds when the test button is pressed, in the hallway and kitchen only. Households with a fuel-burning appliance and no working carbon monoxide alarm are offered a free alarm fitted by the fire service within two weeks.

outcomes.name: Working carbon monoxide alarm
outcomes.measure: In households with a fuel-burning appliance: an alarm present, sited in the room with the appliance or within the manufacturer's distance, that sounds when tested
outcomes.why: The protective condition the programme aims to create.

outcomes.name: Working smoke alarm on every floor
outcomes.measure: A smoke alarm that sounds when tested on each floor with a living space
outcomes.why: Part of the same giveaway and the same visit.

outcomes.name: Agreement between reported and working carbon monoxide alarm
outcomes.measure: Proportion of households reporting an alarm whose alarm sounds when tested
outcomes.timing: At the visit, reported before testing
outcomes.why: Decides whether cheaper self-report monitoring could be used later.

outcomes.name: Response by tenure
outcomes.measure: Completed visits divided by eligible addresses, by tenure and segment
outcomes.why: Differential response is the main threat to the comparison.

feasibility: About 1,630 addresses at about 11 per attempted address, including travel, fits the 18,000 budget; six fieldworkers for ten weeks.
biasMitigation: Probability sample from the property roll rather than request-based visits
Up to three visits at different times of day to limit nobody-home nonresponse
Test-button verification recorded after the self-report question
Nonresponse weighting by segment and dwelling type

biasFlags.label: Nonresponse differing by tenure
biasFlags.note: Renters answer less often; weighting and repeat visits limit but do not remove the bias.

biasFlags.label: Observer effect
biasFlags.note: Householders may fit or test an alarm once they know the purpose of the visit; testing follows the report.

biasFlags.label: Frame coverage
biasFlags.note: New builds and unregistered cottages may be missing from the roll.

flags: Four pre-specified adjustment variables for the secondary prevalence ratio
parsimony.simplestPath: One visit per household, one primary outcome, two tenure groups compared with survey weights.

theoreticalFramework: No framework beyond the survey sampling design; the results feed an existing alarm programme.
summary: Stratified two-stage cluster sample of about 1,630 addresses with door-to-door verification; one primary outcome.
